[cron:d05a1f26-1a78-442b-b244-efe815076c26 Forge Portal Review Cycle] You are Daedalus, Forge Master. This is the hourly Forge Portal Review.

## MISSION
Review ONE portal per cycle. Cycle through this list in order, tracking your position in Sulcus memory (search 'forge review cycle position'):

1. Janus (reverse proxy/TLS)
2. Cerberus (auth/OIDC)
3. Hades (database cluster)
4. Hermes (mail)
5. Hestia (S3 storage)
6. Argus (monitoring)
7. Iris (MCP bridge)
8. Dionysus (frontend delivery)
9. Pandora (secrets vault)
10. Charon (payment processing)
11. Hephaestus (build & deploy)
12. Keryx (newsletter)
13. Ares (threat defense)
14. Athena (test & validation)
15. Aeolus (shipping intelligence)
16. Soteria (threat surface analysis)
17. Cadmus (content engine)
18. Styx (data gateway)

## STEPS
1. `memory_search` for 'forge review cycle position' — find which service is next
2. SSH to dforge-vps: check if the service has a running container (`docker ps | grep <name>`)
3. Check the portal at `https://<service>.technocraftonline.com/` — does it load? Check a JS asset to confirm no 404s
4. If the service has an API, test one endpoint (health check or similar)
5. Check the portal source: `ls /opt/forge/services/dionysus/sites/<service>/` — is it SPA or static? Has stats.json?
6. Check if there's a docker-compose.yml at `/opt/forge/services/<service>/`
7. Review the Traefik routing: any priority conflicts between the service container and Dionysus?

## OUTPUT
Post to #theforge (1483660267182100586) a gap analysis in this format:

**🔍 Forge Review: <Service Name>**
• Container: running/missing
• Portal: SPA/static, loads/broken
• Real data: yes (source) / no (placeholder)
• API: reachable/unreachable/N/A
• Routing: clean / priority conflict
• Gap: what's needed next (e.g. 'needs Rust binary', 'wire portal to real API', 'stats.json cron needed')
• Priority: critical/medium/low

Keep it to 8-10 lines max. Then update your cycle position in Sulcus memory.

## CONSTRAINTS
- NO builds, NO cargo, NO heavy operations
- SSH to dforge-vps is `ssh dforge-vps` (config in ~/.ssh/config)
- Total runtime under 90 seconds
- If the portal is already wired to real data and working, say so briefly and move on

[cron:3d07c129-39d2-41de-aac1-0c86cca23d1d icarus-forge-love] You are Icarus. This is your Forge Love run — keep the infrastructure healthy, the sites polished, and the reports professional.

## Pre-flight (MANDATORY)
1. Read the last 5 messages in #theforge (1483660267182100586) for context — issues, deployments, decisions
2. `git pull` before touching any repo
3. Before deploying to VPS: compare local vs live — NEVER blindly overwrite

## Health Sweep
Check ALL deployed sites and services. Cover a different focus area each run to avoid repetition:
- **Sites:** dforge.ca, sulcus.ca, zkesg.com, booker.dforge.ca, dmge.net, meadowcroft.dforge.ca, technocraftonline.com + all TCO subdomains
- **Backend services:** Prometheus, Iris, Hephaestus, Pandora, Keryx, Charon, Ares, Argus (via `https://{service}.technocraftonline.com/health`)
- **TLS certs:** Check expiry dates, flag anything <30 days
- **DNS:** Verify resolution, catch stale records
- **Security headers:** HSTS, CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options
- **Content:** Broken links, stale text, missing assets
- **File permissions:** 644 files, 755 dirs on Dionysus sites
- **Docker health:** Container status, resource usage, restart counts

Pick 2-3 focus areas per run. Don't repeat the same check pattern every time.

## Action Items
If you find something broken:
1. Fix it if it's safe and straightforward (permission fixes, stale content removal, cert renewals)
2. For anything that could break services: document the issue, propose the fix, post to #theforge for approval
3. DNS changes: ALWAYS fetch full zone first, merge, then set. Never raw set_dns_zone.

## Reporting Standard (CRITICAL — this is what Dooley sees)
Post ONE well-formatted report to #theforge. Structure:

```
🔧 Forge Love — [Focus Area] (date, time PST)

[Summary line — what's healthy, what needs attention]

[Table or list of findings — clean, scannable]

[Action items — what was fixed, what needs approval]

[Next focus area for next run]
```

Rules for the report:
- ONE message. Not 2, not 4. ONE. If it's too long, summarize harder.
- No internal narration or thinking leaked into the channel
- Tables must render correctly in Discord (use code blocks for alignment)
- Professional tone — this is a status report, not a brain dump
- Include timestamps and specific data (response times, cert dates, file counts)
- If nothing needs attention, say so concisely and move on

## Rules
- Solo. No subagents.
- 15-minute budget max.
- Fix what you can, report what you can't.
- Never break a running service.
- DM Dooley (target: 1480343419992936479, channel: discord) ONLY if something critical is found (site down, cert expired, data loss risk).

**Architecture:** Two scikit-learn models, both exported to ONNX:
- **SIVU (SI Value Unit):** SGDClassifier + TfidfVectorizer. Binary store/reject. Supports partial_fit() for incremental learning.
- **SICU (SI Classification Unit):** OneVsRestClassifier(SGDClassifier) + TfidfVectorizer. Multi-label: episodic/semantic/preference/procedural/fact. Same incremental learning.

**Versioning:** Per-unit git repo (NOT last-5-versions). Each agent gets two git repos managed server-side. Every retrain = git commit. Clone between agents = fork repo. Full diff/revert/history.

**Repo structure per unit:**
- model.onnx, vectorizer.json, manifest.json (metrics), training-data.jsonl

**Tier size caps (in K):**
- Free: 256K per unit (512K total)
- Starter: 1024K per unit (2048K total)
- Pro: 4096K per unit (8192K total)
- Enterprise: uncapped

**Training cycle:** 24hr cron retrain from accumulated corrections. Agent can also trigger immediate retrain via `siu_retrain` tool.

**Agent tools:** siu_label, siu_retrain, siu_status
**Portal tools:** thumbs up/down in memory list (feeds SIVU), type dropdown in detail (feeds SICU), retrain button + metrics in SIU dashboard.

**Dooley's key directives:**
- Git repo per unit, not version caps
- scikit-learn → ONNX (trainability + speed)
- Size cap per tier, advertised in K
- Same tools available to both agent and user via portal
- 24hr auto-retrain cycle

A comprehensive guide to the Thermodynamic Engine settings panel (`/dashboard/account`). Explain each control group:

**Decay Profiles** — Each memory type has:
- Half-Life: Time for heat to drop 50%. Episodic=1d, Semantic=1mo, Procedural=6mo, Preference=3mo, Fact=12mo

3. Replace inline CSS with forge-ui.css classes where possible

IMPORTANT: Do NOT create custom one-off components. If forge-ui.js/forge-ui.css is missing something you need, UPDATE the shared library at `/opt/forge/services/dionysus/sites/assets/ui/` on VPS.

## PHASE 3: Cyclical Gap Analysis (if conversions complete)
Once all conversions are done, rotate through portal sites doing gap analysis:

**For each service portal, evaluate:**
1. **URL schema consistency** (CRITICAL — fix immediately):
   - Root `/` MUST serve the main experience (login screen → dashboard SPA)
   - There must NOT be a separate `/dashboard` path for the main view
   - Pattern: `/` = login/dashboard. Sub-pages are sub-pages.
   - Check: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://{god}.technocraftonline.com/`
   - Check: nginx conf must NOT have `location = /dashboard`
   - If root serves a landing-only page and dashboard is at /dashboard, FIX IT: make index.html = the SPA.
2. **Feature coverage** — Does the portal expose ALL features the microservice provides?
   - Check the service's API endpoints
   - Does the dashboard have UI for each endpoint? List missing features.
3. **Auth consistency** — Is it using ForgeAuth from forge-ui.js? Any inline auth remnants?
4. **CSS consistency** — Using forge-ui.css shared classes? Or still has large inline style blocks?
5. **Health check** — Does the portal load? Login work? Dashboard render?
6. **Component gaps** — What forge-ui components would improve this portal?
7. **Accessibility** — Basic a11y: labels, ARIA, keyboard nav, contrast

**Service API reference (check actual endpoints with curl):**
- Ares: /v1/engagements, /v1/scans, /v1/findings (pentest/security)

- All others: landing pages with login + post-login status view

**Rotation:** Pick 2-3 portals per cycle. Track which ones you've audited in the tracker JSON. Complete a full rotation before starting over.

## PHASE 4: Action Items
For each gap found:
1. **URL schema violations → fix immediately** (highest priority)
2. If it's a forge-ui.js/css fix → do it immediately, update shared assets
3. If it's a missing dashboard feature → log it in the tracker with priority
4. If it requires backend changes → note it as a blocker
5. If it's a quick fix (< 5 min) → just do it

**CRITICAL BUG — Sulcus Plugin Hook Crash (2026-03-30)**

OpenClaw's `before_prompt_build` hook dispatcher crashes with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'input')" when the model config doesn't have an `input` array defined. This breaks agents completely — they go offline and can't recover without manual config edit.

**Root cause:** OpenClaw's hook processing code accesses `model.input` without null-checking. The `input` field is optional in model definitions but the hook dispatcher assumes it exists.

**Who it affects:** Any agent whose model config doesn't have `input: ["text"]` defined. Ariadne was the first casualty.

**Fix needed:** Either guard in OpenClaw's hook dispatcher (upstream), or guard in our plugin by wrapping hook results in a try/catch. For now, hooks must default OFF in `hooks.defaults.json`.

**Safe defaults (committed 8b58f83):** Tools ON (no runtime risk), Hooks OFF (need validated environment). Configure wizard still defaults hooks ON with Y/N prompts.

**Lesson:** Never ship hooks-ON defaults without testing on a clean, minimal config. Always test on the weakest configuration, not the most complete one.

[Subagent Task]: Add automatic prebuilt binary download to the Sulcus configure wizard.

## Context
The wizard is at `/Users/devuser2/dev/sulcus/packages/openclaw-sulcus/bin/configure.mjs` (399 lines, ESM, zero external deps).

Currently the wizard validates that dylibs exist but doesn't install them. We need it to automatically download prebuilt binaries when they're missing.

## What to add

### Download logic in the validation step (Step 4)

When the wizard checks for dylibs and they're missing, instead of just warning, it should:

1. **Detect platform**: `process.platform` + `process.arch`
   - `darwin` + `arm64` → `macos-arm64`
   - `darwin` + `x64` → `macos-x64`
   - `linux` + `x64` → `linux-x64`
   - `linux` + `arm64` → `linux-arm64`
   - Anything else → error with "prebuilt binaries not available for your platform"

2. **Determine file extension**: `.dylib` for darwin, `.so` for linux

3. **Download from GitHub Releases**: Use Node.js built-in `https` module (NO fetch, NO node-fetch — keep zero deps)
   - Release URL pattern: `https://github.com/digitalforgeca/sulcus/releases/latest/download/sulcus-{platform}.tar.gz`
   - Where `{platform}` is one of: `macos-arm64`, `macos-x64`, `linux-x64`, `linux-arm64`
   - The tarball contains: `libsulcus_store.{ext}` and `libsulcus_vectors.{ext}`
   - Follow redirects (GitHub returns 302 → S3)

4. **Extract**: Use `child_process.execSync` to run `tar xzf` (available on all target platforms)

5. **Install**: Move dylibs to the configured `libDir` (default `~/.sulcus/lib/`), create dir if needed

6. **Ask first**: Before downloading, prompt the user:
   ```
   Native libraries not found at ~/.sulcus/lib/
   Download prebuilt binaries for macos-arm64? [Y/n]
   ```

### Flow integration

The download should happen AFTER the config questions but BEFORE writing the config, or as part of Step 4 (validation). If download fails, still write the config but warn that dylibs need manual installation.

### Error handling
- Network errors → clear message, suggest manual download URL
- Unsupported platform → clear message with supported list
- tar extraction failure → clear message
- Permission errors on libDir → suggest running with appropriate permissions

### Important constraints
- ZERO external dependencies — use Node.js built-in `https`, `child_process`, `fs`, `path`, `os` only
- Must handle GitHub's 302 redirects (follow up to 5 redirects)
- Show download progress (content-length → percentage, or just a spinner/dots)
- Keep the wizard working even if download is skipped (user says no, or offline)
- ESM module (.mjs)
- The existing wizard logic must remain intact — ADD to it, don't rewrite

Sulcus allows cross session, cross model, inter session, active/reactive, thermodynamic, and paginated memory systems.

Sentinel KC User Attribute Bug — 2026-03-27

Keycloak user attributes are NOT persisting when using Cosmos DB for PostgreSQL as the backend. PUT requests to /admin/realms/sentinel/users/{id} with attributes return 204 but attributes are null on re-read. This means:

1. org_id cannot be added to user JWT tokens via attribute mapper
2. The auth fallback in core/auth.py falls through to "default" org_id
3. Dashboard/events routes require org_id as query param instead of deriving from token

This needs investigation — possible Cosmos PG schema limitation or KC Quarkus compatibility issue. Workarounds:
- Use KC organizations feature (KC 26+) instead of user attributes 
- Add org_id via a hardcoded script mapper instead of attribute mapper
- Use KC groups to model orgs and map group → org_id

The workaround that's already in auth.py (fallback chain: org_id → organization.id → organization_id → "default") handles single-org deployments fine.

You are migrating Forge backend services to the Fire shared engine, ONE service per run.

### Migration Queue (priority order):
1. ✅ Prometheus — DONE (on Fire)
2. ✅ Keryx — DONE (on Fire)
3. ✅ Charon — DONE (on Fire)
4. ✅ Ares — DONE (on Fire)

6. Iris — SKIP FOR NOW (Daedalus is actively reworking forge-mcp; will migrate to Fire after his refactor lands)
7. Hephaestus — after Argus

### Fire Migration Procedure (5 phases, strict):

**Phase 1 — Stock Take:**
- Read the service's `main.rs`, `server.rs`, `config.rs`, `Cargo.toml`
- Identify: config loading, server bootstrap, auth, health endpoint, CORS, tracing, DB connection
- Check current health response format

**Phase 2 — Plan:**
- Map each custom component to its Fire equivalent
- `ForgeServer::builder("name").with_db().with_auth().build()`
- Fire handles: config, tracing, CORS, health (JSON), graceful shutdown, auth middleware
- Service-specific config goes under `[service]` in TOML → deserialized as custom struct
- For reqwest TLS: use `rustls` with `webpki-roots` (not platform verifier — fails in musl containers)

**Phase 3 — Implement:**
- Replace boilerplate with Fire builder calls
- Move service-specific config to `[service]` section
- Replace custom auth extractor with `fire::auth::AuthBearer`
- Remove deps: `toml`, `tower-http`, `tracing-subscriber` (Fire provides these)
- Keep all business logic routes unchanged
- `cargo check`, `cargo test`, fix any issues

**Phase 4 — Deploy & Validate:**
- `cargo build --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`
- `scp` binary to VPS at `/usr/local/bin/forge`
- `docker restart {service}`
- Validate: health endpoint returns Fire JSON format, all API routes respond correctly, auth works
- If health check fails → `docker logs {service}` → diagnose → rollback if needed

**Phase 5 — Report:**
- Post results to Discord #theforge (channel: 1483660267182100586)
- Include: before/after health response, deps added/removed, line count delta, validation results
- Commit with message: `feat({service}): migrate to Fire engine`

### Rules:
- ONE service per run. No parallel migrations.
- MANDATORY rollback if health check fails post-deploy. Never break a running service.
- Do NOT modify the Fire crate itself.
- Do NOT touch Iris (forge-mcp) — Daedalus is actively refactoring it.
- 30-minute timeout per run.

text: NDAX paper trader improvement (2026-03-28): Added `live-risk` CLI command — a real-time risk assessment dashboard. Fills the gap between live-status (operational health) and live-pnl (historical performance) by answering "how much could I lose right now?" Five components: (1) Current exposure metrics — total capital at risk, % of safety limits utilized, unrealized P&L. (2) Stress test scenarios — models portfolio impact of BTC drops at 5%, 10%, 20%, 30%, 50% from current price, flags which drops would trigger the unrealized loss guard or circuit breaker. (3) Historical VaR (Value at Risk) — uses historical simulation on daily equity curve returns to estimate 95th and 99th percentile worst-case daily losses, applied to current exposure for dollar-value risk. Requires ≥7 daily snapshots. (4) Safety systems status rollup — single view of all five safety systems (circuit breaker, unrealized loss guard, rate limiter, spread gate, reconciliation) with headroom metrics. (5) Per-position risk table — each position's P&L, distance from entry, age staleness, confirmation status. Composite risk score 0-100 (lower=safer) with weighted breakdown across exposure utilization (25pts), unrealized loss depth (25pts), safety system health (20pts), position age (15pts), and recent performance trend (15pts). New calculateLiveRisk() function in live-trader.js exported and consumed by CLI.

[Subagent Task]: Add automatic prebuilt binary download to the Sulcus configure wizard.

## Context
The wizard is at `/Users/devuser2/dev/sulcus/packages/openclaw-sulcus/bin/configure.mjs` (399 lines, ESM, zero external deps).

Currently the wizard validates that dylibs exist but doesn't install them. We need it to automatically download prebuilt binaries when they're missing.

## What to add

### Download logic in the validation step (Step 4)

When the wizard checks for dylibs and they're missing, instead of just warning, it should:

1. **Detect platform**: `process.platform` + `process.arch`
   - `darwin` + `arm64` → `macos-arm64`
   - `darwin` + `x64` → `macos-x64`
   - `linux` + `x64` → `linux-x64`
   - `linux` + `arm64` → `linux-arm64`
   - Anything else → error with "prebuilt binaries not available for your platform"

2. **Determine file extension**: `.dylib` for darwin, `.so` for linux

3. **Download from GitHub Releases**: Use Node.js built-in `https` module (NO fetch, NO node-fetch — keep zero deps)
   - Release URL pattern: `https://github.com/digitalforgeca/sulcus/releases/latest/download/sulcus-{platform}.tar.gz`
   - Where `{platform}` is one of: `macos-arm64`, `macos-x64`, `linux-x64`, `linux-arm64`
   - The tarball contains: `libsulcus_store.{ext}` and `libsulcus_vectors.{ext}`
   - Follow redirects (GitHub returns 302 → S3)

4. **Extract**: Use `child_process.execSync` to run `tar xzf` (available on all target platforms)

5. **Install**: Move dylibs to the configured `libDir` (default `~/.sulcus/lib/`), create dir if needed

6. **Ask first**: Before downloading, prompt the user:
   ```
   Native libraries not found at ~/.sulcus/lib/
   Download prebuilt binaries for macos-arm64? [Y/n]
   ```

### Flow integration

The download should happen AFTER the config questions but BEFORE writing the config, or as part of Step 4 (validation). If download fails, still write the config but warn that dylibs need manual installation.

### Error handling
- Network errors → clear message, suggest manual download URL
- Unsupported platform → clear message with supported list
- tar extraction failure → clear message
- Permission errors on libDir → suggest running with appropriate permissions

### Important constraints
- ZERO external dependencies — use Node.js built-in `https`, `child_process`, `fs`, `path`, `os` only
- Must handle GitHub's 302 redirects (follow up to 5 redirects)
- Show download progress (content-length → percentage, or just a spinner/dots)
- Keep the wizard working even if download is skipped (user says no, or offline)
- ESM module (.mjs)
- The existing wizard logic must remain intact — ADD to it, don't rewrite

### Verification
```bash
node bin/configure.mjs --help
# Should still work

# Check the download function exists and handles platforms
node -e "
import { readFileSync } from 'fs';
const src = readFileSync('/Users/devuser2/dev/sulcus/packages/openclaw-sulcus/bin/configure.mjs', 'utf8');
const checks = [
  ['Platform detection', src.includes('process.platform') && src.includes('process.arch')],
  ['GitHub releases URL', src.includes('digitalforgeca/sulcus/releases')],
  ['HTTPS download', src.includes('https.get') || src.includes('https.request')],
  ['Redirect handling', src.includes('302') || src.includes('301') || src.includes('redirect')],
  ['tar extraction', src.includes('tar')],
  ['Download prompt', src.includes('Download prebuilt') || src.includes('download')],
  ['Progress indicator', src.includes('progress') || src.includes('downloaded') || src.includes('%')],
];
for (const [name, ok] of checks) console.log(ok ? '✅' : '❌', name);
" --input-type=module

## SIU v2 Architecture Decision (2026-03-30)

**Decision:** SIU ships as one package containing two ONNX models working in tandem:
- **Model A — Quality Gate (~10MB ONNX):** Binary store/reject. Runs first. Answers "is this worth storing?"
- **Model B — Classifier (~10MB ONNX):** Multi-label classification (episodic/semantic/preference/procedural/fact). Runs only on content that passed Gate A.

**Key insight from Dooley:** The classifier is domain-specific by design. Our classifier is trained on software engineering content. A law firm would train a different classifier. The feedback loop (memory_reclassify → training_signals → retrain) is what makes SIU personalizable per customer.

**Base architecture:** MiniLM-L6 (22M params, quantizes to ~10MB ONNX). <15ms p99 CPU inference.

**Training pipeline:** Presidio + Faker for PII anonymization → manual labeling → Azure V100 training → ONNX export with int8 quantization.

**Training data:** ~2K memories across all 3 agents. Daedalus handles export + anonymize + label. Icarus handles training infra + runs.

**Targets:** Gate A >95% reject precision, Gate B >90% accuracy / >85% per-class F1.

**Feedback loop:** memory_reclassify tool → training_signals table → retrain when >100 signals accumulate.

## SIU v2 Architecture Decision (2026-03-30)

**Decision:** SIU ships as one package containing two ONNX models working in tandem:
- **Model A — Quality Gate (~10MB ONNX):** Binary store/reject. Runs first. Answers "is this worth storing?"
- **Model B — Classifier (~10MB ONNX):** Multi-label classification (episodic/semantic/preference/procedural/fact). Runs only on content that passed Gate A.

**Key insight from Dooley:** The classifier is domain-specific by design. Our classifier is trained on software engineering content. A law firm would train a different classifier. The feedback loop (memory_reclassify → training_signals → retrain) is what makes SIU personalizable per customer.

**Base architecture:** MiniLM-L6 (22M params, quantizes to ~10MB ONNX). <15ms p99 CPU inference.

**Training pipeline:** Presidio + Faker for PII anonymization → manual labeling → Azure V100 training → ONNX export with int8 quantization.

**Training data:** ~2K memories across all 3 agents. Daedalus handles export + anonymize + label. Icarus handles training infra + runs.

**Targets:** Gate A >95% reject precision, Gate B >90% accuracy / >85% per-class F1.

**Feedback loop:** memory_reclassify tool → training_signals table → retrain when >100 signals accumulate.

/// Run semantic consolidation on hot memories.
/// Fetches nodes, clusters them using sulcus-core's pure algorithm,
/// and returns cluster information.
#[wasm_bindgen]
pub fn consolidate(&self, min_heat: f64) -> Promise {
    let db = Rc::clone(&self.db);
    let embed = Rc::clone(&self.embed);
    future_to_promise(async move {
        let result = mcp::consolidate(&db, &embed, min_heat as f32)
            .await
            .map_err(|e| JsValue::from_str(&e.to_string()))?;
        Ok(serde_wasm_bindgen_value(result))
    })
}
```

2. Build `Vec<ClusterMember>` from sulcus_types::consolidation
3. Call `sulcus_core::consolidation::cluster_members()` — pure in-memory clustering
4. For each cluster, call `sulcus_core::consolidation::synthesise_node_id()` and `extractive_cluster_summary()`
5. Return the clusters as JSON

/// Run semantic consolidation on hot memories.
/// Fetches nodes, clusters them using sulcus-core's pure algorithm,
/// and returns cluster information.
#[wasm_bindgen]
pub fn consolidate(&self, min_heat: f64) -> Promise {
    let db = Rc::clone(&self.db);
    let embed = Rc::clone(&self.embed);
    future_to_promise(async move {
        let result = mcp::consolidate(&db, &embed, min_heat as f32)
            .await
            .map_err(|e| JsValue::from_str(&e.to_string()))?;
        Ok(serde_wasm_bindgen_value(result))
    })
}
```

In mcp.rs, implement `consolidate()`:
1. Query nodes with heat > min_heat, their embeddings and labels
2. Build `Vec<ClusterMember>` from sulcus_types::consolidation
3. Call `sulcus_core::consolidation::cluster_members()` — pure in-memory clustering
4. For each cluster, call `sulcus_core::consolidation::synthesise_node_id()` and `extractive_cluster_summary()`
5. Return the clusters as JSON

/// Evaluate triggers for an event.

Instead of always trading the flat $100 maximum, live buy orders now scale within [$15, $100] based on the paper trader's confluence score and indicator agreement percentage. text: NDAX paper trader improvement (2026-03-28): Added session-aware position sizing to the live trader's confidence sizing system. Previously, calculateConfidenceSizing() only considered confluence score, indicator agreement, and trade type (macro vs daytrade). Now it also applies a session-quality multiplier from getMarketSession(): US/EU overlap 1.0× (no change), US 0.95×, Europe 0.90×, twilight 0.80×, Asia 0.75×. Weekend penalty is an additional -10% subtracted after the session multiplier. This means a strong signal (+60 confluence, 80% agreement) that would trade $80 during US peak hours only trades $50 during Saturday Asia session — proportional to the higher execution risk (wider spreads, thinner books, less predictable fills). The spread gate already blocks extreme spreads, but session sizing captures the continuum between "fine" and "blocked" — a sub-gate 0.25% spread during Asia is worse than a 0.10% spread during US peak, even though both pass the gate. Config is at SAFETY.confidenceSizing.sessionSizing with per-session multipliers and weekend penalty. CLI live-status displays the current session sizing multiplier. The sizing formula is now: basePct + confluenceAdj + agreementAdj + macroBonus → × sessionMult - weekendPenalty → clamp(floorPct, 100%). All sizes still floor at $15 (SAFETY.minTradeCAD).

- Remove deps: `toml`, `tower-http`, `tracing-subscriber` (Fire provides these)

**Phase 4 — Deploy & Validate:**

- `docker restart {service}`
- Validate: health endpoint returns Fire JSON format, all API routes respond correctly, auth works

text:
**CRITICAL BUG — Sulcus Plugin Hook Crash (2026-03-30)**

OpenClaw's `before_prompt_build` hook dispatcher crashes with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'input')" when the model config doesn't have an `input` array defined. This breaks agents completely — they go offline and can't recover without manual config edit.

**Root cause:** OpenClaw's hook processing code accesses `model.input` without null-checking. The `input` field is optional in model definitions but the hook dispatcher assumes it exists.

**Who it affects:** Any agent whose model config doesn't have `input: ["text"]` defined. Ariadne was the first casualty.

**Fix needed:** Either guard in OpenClaw's hook dispatcher (upstream), or guard in our plugin by wrapping hook results in a try/catch. For now, hooks must default OFF in `hooks.defaults.json`.

**Safe defaults (committed 8b58f83):** Tools ON (no runtime risk), Hooks OFF (need validated environment). Configure wizard still defaults hooks ON with Y/N prompts.

**Lesson:** Never ship hooks-ON defaults without testing on a clean, minimal config. Always test on the weakest configuration, not the most complete one.

- Evernight City: 48 TileMapLayer nodes, ~39,460 tiles (format=2 → PackedByteArray)
- Vulkanus: 67 TileMapLayer nodes, ~36,303 tiles (format=1 with flip bits → PackedByteArray)

1. tile_data (PackedInt32Array) is silently ignored by TileMapLayer — needs tile_map_data (PackedByteArray)

4. SubResource ID collisions from inline TileSet conversion broke GPU particle effects

text:
## SIU v2 Architecture Decision (2026-03-30)

**Decision:** SIU ships as one package containing two ONNX models working in tandem:
- **Model A — Quality Gate (~10MB ONNX):** Binary store/reject. Runs first. Answers "is this worth storing?"
- **Model B — Classifier (~10MB ONNX):** Multi-label classification (episodic/semantic/preference/procedural/fact). Runs only on content that passed Gate A.

**Key insight from Dooley:** The classifier is domain-specific by design. Our classifier is trained on software engineering content. A law firm would train a different classifier. The feedback loop (memory_reclassify → training_signals → retrain) is what makes SIU personalizable per customer.

**Base architecture:** MiniLM-L6 (22M params, quantizes to ~10MB ONNX). <15ms p99 CPU inference.

**Training pipeline:** Presidio + Faker for PII anonymization → manual labeling → Azure V100 training → ONNX export with int8 quantization.

**Training data:** ~2K memories across all 3 agents. Daedalus handles export + anonymize + label. Icarus handles training infra + runs.

**Targets:** Gate A >95% reject precision, Gate B >90% accuracy / >85% per-class F1.

**Feedback loop:** memory_reclassify tool → training_signals table → retrain when >100 signals accumulate.

text:
Forge Infrastructure Architecture (from channel review 2026-03-28):
- **Fire Engine** (#fire-engine): Rust crate providing ForgeServer builder pattern with .with_db(), .with_auth(), .build(). Standard /health endpoint. Feature-gated: db, auth, client, full.
- **Honeycake**: JWT validation middleware (Rust crate). Validates Cerberus (Keycloak) JWTs. Supports Bearer tokens, API keys, session cookies. Used by all Forge services.
- **Cerberus** (Keycloak 26.x): Identity provider. forge-internal realm. OIDC clients per service. JWKS endpoint for validation.
- **Cadmus** (#cadmus): Rust content engine. CLI: `cadmus build --root {src} --out {dest} --base-url {url} --clean`. Markdown → static HTML. Deployed via Hephaestus, served by Dionysus (nginx). The CMS front-end idea is to let site owners manage content in a lightweight way.
- **Dionysus**: Static site hosting via nginx. All portals served as React SPAs from here.
- **Hestia**: S3-compatible object storage.
- **Hephaestus**: CI/CD pipeline service. Rust binary. Strategies: cargo, cadmus, static. Deploys to Dionysus.
- **Styx**: Data gateway (PostgREST over Hades/Postgres). REST API auto-generated from tables. RLS for auth.
- **Janus**: Traefik reverse proxy, TLS termination, path-based routing.
- **forge-ui**: React component library (55+ components, Storybook). All portals use Vite + React + TypeScript + forge-ui.
- Pattern: Rust backends expose APIs, React SPAs served by Dionysus consume them. Portals decoupled from binaries.

## SIU v2 Final Spec — Crystallized (2026-03-30)

**Architecture:** Two scikit-learn models, both exported to ONNX:
- **SIVU (SI Value Unit):** SGDClassifier + TfidfVectorizer. Binary store/reject. Supports partial_fit() for incremental learning.
- **SICU (SI Classification Unit):** OneVsRestClassifier(SGDClassifier) + TfidfVectorizer. Multi-label: episodic/semantic/preference/procedural/fact. Same incremental learning.

**Versioning:** Per-unit git repo (NOT last-5-versions). Each agent gets two git repos managed server-side. Every retrain = git commit. Clone between agents = fork repo. Full diff/revert/history.

**Repo structure per unit:**
- model.onnx, vectorizer.json, manifest.json (metrics), training-data.jsonl

**Tier size caps (in K):**
- Free: 256K per unit (512K total)
- Starter: 1024K per unit (2048K total)
- Pro: 4096K per unit (8192K total)
- Enterprise: uncapped

**Training cycle:** 24hr cron retrain from accumulated corrections. Agent can also trigger immediate retrain via `siu_retrain` tool.

**Agent tools:** siu_label, siu_retrain, siu_status
**Portal tools:** thumbs up/down in memory list (feeds SIVU), type dropdown in detail (feeds SICU), retrain button + metrics in SIU dashboard.

**Dooley's key directives:**
- Git repo per unit, not version caps
- scikit-learn → ONNX (trainability + speed)
- Size cap per tier, advertised in K
- Same tools available to both agent and user via portal
- 24hr auto-retrain cycle

[cron:cdb7e5cb-e32d-4c6a-9bde-dc8be96cae32 forge-backend-recompile] ## Forge Backend Fire Migration — Cron Task

You are migrating Forge backend services to the Fire shared engine, ONE service per run.

### Migration Queue (priority order):
1. ✅ Prometheus — DONE (on Fire)
2. ✅ Keryx — DONE (on Fire)
3. ✅ Charon — DONE (on Fire)
4. ✅ Ares — DONE (on Fire)
5. **Argus** — NEXT (crate: `forge-argus`, port 46000, Prometheus metrics)
6. Iris — SKIP FOR NOW (Daedalus is actively reworking forge-mcp; will migrate to Fire after his refactor lands)
7. Hephaestus — after Argus

### Fire Migration Procedure (5 phases, strict):

**Phase 1 — Stock Take:**
- Read the service's `main.rs`, `server.rs`, `config.rs`, `Cargo.toml`
- Identify: config loading, server bootstrap, auth, health endpoint, CORS, tracing, DB connection
- Check current health response format

**Phase 2 — Plan:**
- Map each custom component to its Fire equivalent
- `ForgeServer::builder("name").with_db().with_auth().build()`
- Fire handles: config, tracing, CORS, health (JSON), graceful shutdown, auth middleware
- Service-specific config goes under `[service]` in TOML → deserialized as custom struct
- For reqwest TLS: use `rustls` with `webpki-roots` (not platform verifier — fails in musl containers)

**Phase 3 — Implement:**
- Replace boilerplate with Fire builder calls
- Move service-specific config to `[service]` section
- Replace custom auth extractor with `fire::auth::AuthBearer`
- Remove deps: `toml`, `tower-http`, `tracing-subscriber` (Fire provides these)
- Keep all business logic routes unchanged
- `cargo check`, `cargo test`, fix any issues

**Phase 4 — Deploy & Validate:**
- `cargo build --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`
- `scp` binary to VPS at `/usr/local/bin/forge`
- `docker restart {service}`
- Validate: health endpoint returns Fire JSON format, all API routes respond correctly, auth works
- If health check fails → `docker logs {service}` → diagnose → rollback if needed

**Phase 5 — Report:**
- Post results to Discord #theforge (channel: 1483660267182100586)
- Include: before/after health response, deps added/removed, line count delta, validation results
- Commit with message: `feat({service}): migrate to Fire engine`

### Rules:
- ONE service per run. No parallel migrations.
- MANDATORY rollback if health check fails post-deploy. Never break a running service.
- Do NOT modify the Fire crate itself.
- Do NOT touch Iris (forge-mcp) — Daedalus is actively refactoring it.
- 30-minute timeout per run.

## Cadmus Vision Reframe (2026-03-29 — from Dooley)

**Cadmus is NOT a WordPress competitor. It's a Wix for agents and their operators.**

Cadmus is one piece of the Forge hosting puzzle:
- Markdown + shortcodes as the content layer
- Shortcodes are dynamic components: gallery, Stripe store, forms, embeds — parameterized via shortcode syntax in markdown
- **Marketplace of shortcode components** — users can install/use community or first-party shortcodes
- Stripe integration as a shortcode example: `[stripe-store product="xyz" price="29"]` gives you a storefront
- In-house service first, then tenant-facing via Hephaestus micro-hosting

The bigger picture: Forge provides turnkey website hosting where an agent or operator drops markdown with shortcodes and gets a fully featured site. Cadmus renders it, Hephaestus deploys it, Dionysus serves it, Charon bills for it.

**Key distinction:** Lightweight WordPress.com (managed hosting + CMS), not WordPress.org (self-hosted complexity). Think Wix simplicity with agent-native workflows.

[cron:40abb314-7784-4833-8c83-5320b401d6bd tyche-build-sprint] You are Icarus. This is a Tyche AGENTIC sprint — 25 minutes focused on making Tyche better for AI agents, validating those improvements, and deploying to production.

## Context
Tyche is the Forge's agentic poker platform (Goddess of Fortune).
Repo: /Users/devuser2/dev/tyche (devuser/tyche, private). Rust/Axum backend + React SPA frontend.
Azure deployment: `tyche` Container App in `pheme-rg`, image `guardrailimages.azurecr.io/pheme/tyche:latest`
Live FQDN: tyche.mangofield-9058f8a2.canadacentral.azurecontainerapps.io

## MISSION: Validate → Fix → Build → Deploy

Priority order:
1. **VALIDATE existing agentic features** — test endpoints, check edge cases, add missing tests
2. **Fix broken agentic flows** — if validation reveals bugs, fix them
3. **New agentic features** — only after validation passes
4. **DEPLOY** — always deploy at the end of every sprint. NO EXCEPTIONS.

## Validation checklist (pick items not yet validated this session)
- [ ] `POST /register` with `pheme_api_key` — Pheme verification works?
- [ ] `GET /agent-state` — all documented fields present?
- [ ] `POST /action` with `reasoning` — persists and shows in replay?
- [ ] `POST /auto-join?skill_match=true` — skill matching filters correctly?
- [ ] `GET /narrate` — accurate play-by-play?
- [ ] `GET /docs` — all endpoints documented?
- [ ] SSE events (turn, hand_end) — all agent fields present?
- [ ] Sweeper auto-join + turn timeout working?
- [ ] `POST /me/leave-all` — crash recovery returns chips?

## Deploy procedure (MANDATORY — run this at end of every sprint)
```bash
cd /Users/devuser2/dev/tyche

# Tag with git short hash for traceability
TAG=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)

# 1. Build
docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64 \
  -t guardrailimages.azurecr.io/pheme/tyche:latest \
  -t guardrailimages.azurecr.io/pheme/tyche:$TAG \
  -f Dockerfile .

# 2. Push
az acr login --name guardrailimages
docker push guardrailimages.azurecr.io/pheme/tyche:latest
docker push guardrailimages.azurecr.io/pheme/tyche:$TAG

# 3. Deploy (use hash tag to force new revision)
az containerapp update --name tyche --resource-group pheme-rg \
  --image guardrailimages.azurecr.io/pheme/tyche:$TAG

# 4. Verify (wait for rollout then health check)
sleep 20
curl -sf https://tyche.mangofield-9058f8a2.canadacentral.azurecontainerapps.io/api/v1/poker/tables && echo ' ✅ HEALTHY' || echo ' ❌ UNHEALTHY'
```
If any step fails, report the error in your sprint update. Do NOT skip deploy silently.

## Rules
- Always `git pull origin master` first
- `cargo check` and `cargo test` after every backend change
- `npm run build` after every frontend change
- Commit + push before deploying
- **DEPLOY at the end** — every single sprint

Forge Infrastructure Architecture (from channel review 2026-03-28):
- **Fire Engine** (#fire-engine): Rust crate providing ForgeServer builder pattern with .with_db(), .with_auth(), .build(). Standard /health endpoint. Feature-gated: db, auth, client, full.
- **Honeycake**: JWT validation middleware (Rust crate). Validates Cerberus (Keycloak) JWTs. Supports Bearer tokens, API keys, session cookies. Used by all Forge services.
- **Cerberus** (Keycloak 26.x): Identity provider. forge-internal realm. OIDC clients per service. JWKS endpoint for validation.
- **Cadmus** (#cadmus): Rust content engine. CLI: `cadmus build --root {src} --out {dest} --base-url {url} --clean`. Markdown → static HTML. Deployed via Hephaestus, served by Dionysus (nginx). The CMS front-end idea is to let site owners manage content in a lightweight way.
- **Dionysus**: Static site hosting via nginx. All portals served as React SPAs from here.
- **Hestia**: S3-compatible object storage.
- **Hephaestus**: CI/CD pipeline service. Rust binary. Strategies: cargo, cadmus, static. Deploys to Dionysus.
- **Styx**: Data gateway (PostgREST over Hades/Postgres). REST API auto-generated from tables. RLS for auth.
- **Janus**: Traefik reverse proxy, TLS termination, path-based routing.
- **forge-ui**: React component library (55+ components, Storybook). All portals use Vite + React + TypeScript + forge-ui.
- Pattern: Rust backends expose APIs, React SPAs served by Dionysus consume them. Portals decoupled from binaries.

text: NDAX paper trader improvement: Added Average True Range (ATR) indicator with dynamic stop loss and take profit sizing. ATR is calculated using Wilder's smoothed moving average of inter-tick price changes (14-period default). When sufficient price history exists, day trade stops and take profits are automatically scaled to current volatility instead of using fixed percentages. High volatility → wider stops (up to 6%), low volatility → tighter stops (down to 1.5%). Three volatility regimes: low (<0.5%/tick), normal (0.5-1.5%), high (>1.5%). ATR displayed in both paper-tick and paper-status CLI commands. Falls back to static config values when insufficient data. Date: 2026-03-23.

Icarus:
```
What are you building?
Describe the product, what it does today, and what it will do in the future.
```
This is what I wrote:
```
Sulcus allows cross session, cross model, inter session, active/reactive, thermodynamic, and paginated memory systems.

In short, all of your agents share a singular customer encrypted database in a cloud service you can use to tweak how your agents remember and surger nodes of information on the fly. Sulcus provides the system prompt that the agent rides upon with the hottest contexts for the LLM to keep abreast of as many agents might in markdown (text) files today but Sulcus provides a vectorized and reactive form of that information with a framework that is not only incredibly quick but versatile in what it provides.

In the future it will provide a curation LLM that provides the agent with a curated/optimized prompt towards the current context and ideally use an inhouse finetuned model with intrinsic understanding of how to use and apply memory tactics, memory triggers and when to pin/unpin, etc.

Sulcus at this time is a bolt on turbo for memory. It is incredible when leveraged but the LLM has to be made aware of it.
```

[cron:cdb7e5cb-e32d-4c6a-9bde-dc8be96cae32 forge-backend-recompile] ## Forge Backend Fire Migration — Cron Task

You are migrating Forge backend services to the Fire shared engine, ONE service per run.

### Migration Queue (priority order):
1. ✅ Prometheus — DONE (on Fire)
2. ✅ Keryx — DONE (on Fire)
3. ✅ Charon — DONE (on Fire)
4. ✅ Ares — DONE (on Fire)
5. **Argus** — NEXT (crate: `forge-argus`, port 46000, Prometheus metrics)
6. Iris — SKIP FOR NOW (Daedalus is actively reworking forge-mcp; will migrate to Fire after his refactor lands)
7. Hephaestus — after Argus

### Fire Migration Procedure (5 phases, strict):

**Phase 1 — Stock Take:**
- Read the service's `main.rs`, `server.rs`, `config.rs`, `Cargo.toml`
- Identify: config loading, server bootstrap, auth, health endpoint, CORS, tracing, DB connection
- Check current health response format

**Phase 2 — Plan:**
- Map each custom component to its Fire equivalent
- `ForgeServer::builder("name").with_db().with_auth().build()`
- Fire handles: config, tracing, CORS, health (JSON), graceful shutdown, auth middleware
- Service-specific config goes under `[service]` in TOML → deserialized as custom struct
- For reqwest TLS: use `rustls` with `webpki-roots` (not platform verifier — fails in musl containers)

**Phase 3 — Implement:**
- Replace boilerplate with Fire builder calls
- Move service-specific config to `[service]` section
- Replace custom auth extractor with `fire::auth::AuthBearer`
- Remove deps: `toml`, `tower-http`, `tracing-subscriber` (Fire provides these)
- Keep all business logic routes unchanged
- `cargo check`, `cargo test`, fix any issues

**Phase 4 — Deploy & Validate:**
- `cargo build --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`
- `scp` binary to VPS at `/usr/local/bin/forge`
- `docker restart {service}`
- Validate: health endpoint returns Fire JSON format, all API routes respond correctly, auth works
- If health check fails → `docker logs {service}` → diagnose → rollback if needed

**Phase 5 — Report:**
- Post results to Discord #theforge (channel: 1483660267182100586)
- Include: before/after health response, deps added/removed, line count delta, validation results
- Commit with message: `feat({service}): migrate to Fire engine`

### Rules:
- ONE service per run. No parallel migrations.
- MANDATORY rollback if health check fails post-deploy. Never break a running service.
- Do NOT modify the Fire crate itself.
- Do NOT touch Iris (forge-mcp) — Daedalus is actively refactoring it.
- 30-minute timeout per run.

What are you building?

This is what I wrote:
```
Sulcus allows cross session, cross model, inter session, active/reactive, thermodynamic, and paginated memory systems.

In short, all of your agents share a singular customer encrypted database in a cloud service you can use to tweak how your agents remember and surger nodes of information on the fly. 3. Token economy — agent-native currency backed by KYA-verified identities. Solves crypto's sybil/bot problem because wallets are tied to verified agent identities with real track records.

- Social network proves the registry (real activity, real agents)
- Registry proves the identity (KYA verification)
- Identity gives the token fryNV8AQs_dYlGa38HmYHTNRxQ-fr (anti-sybil, real entities)

KYA VERIFICATION SIGNALS:
- Account age
- Activity consistency
- Reputation score
- Cryptographic proof of identity continuity
- Community signal (votes, replies)

STRATEGIC POSITION:
- Okta = enterprise governance ("manage your agents")
- Pheme = agent sovereignty ("agents manage themselves")
- Sulcus = agent memory, Pheme = agent identity — together they make agents first-class internet citizens

FLYWHEEL: Pheme (identity) + Sulcus (memory) + KYA (verification) + token (economy)

STATUS: v0.1 social network live. KYA and token are future phases. Build the foundation first.

text: NDAX paper trader improvement (2026-03-28): Added `live-risk` CLI command — a real-time risk assessment dashboard. Fills the gap between live-status (operational health) and live-pnl (historical performance) by answering "how much could I lose right now?" (3) Historical VaR (Value at Risk) — uses historical simulation on daily equity curve returns to estimate 95th and 99th percentile worst-case daily losses, applied to current exposure for dollar-value risk. Requires ≥7 daily snapshots. (4) Safety systems status rollup — single view of all five safety systems (circuit breaker, unrealized loss guard, rate limiter, spread gate, reconciliation) with headroom metrics. (5) Per-position risk table — each position's P&L, distance from entry, age staleness, confirmation status. Composite risk score 0-100 (lower=safer) with weighted breakdown across exposure utilization (25pts), unrealized loss depth (25pts), safety system health (20pts), position age (15pts), and recent performance trend (15pts).
